In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No 2878 of 2024
 (Arising out of Slp (Crl) No 3841 of 2022)
 Shweta Belwal 
 Versus
 State of Uttarakhand and Another 
 Order
1 Leave granted.

2 This appeal arises from the order dated 29 October 2021 passed by the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital in Criminal Miscellaneous Application No 1511 of 2021, by which the High Court rejected the said application filed by the appellant herein invoking the inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 for the purpose of quashing the proceedings of Criminal Case No 3376 of 2021, pending in the court of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haldwani, District Nainital for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471,
120-B of Indian Penal Code.
3

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haldwani, District Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The High Court by its impugned order rejected the application and thereby 4 We have heard Mr Sidharth Luthra, the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant and Mr Dinesh Chander Trehan, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No 2 (the original complainant) and Mr Abhishek Atrey, the learned counsel appearing for the State of Uttarakhand.

5 When the matter was taken up for hearing, Mr Sidharth Luthra had manifold contentions to canvass to make good his case that the criminal proceedings instituted against her client is nothing but an abuse of process of law.
According to the learned senior counsel, no case is made out to put the appellant to trial for the alleged offence.
According to him, the criminal proceedings instituted against the petitioner is nothing but a counter blast to the civil suit filed by one Pankaj Malik.

6 On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No 2 submitted that no error much less an error of law could be said to have been committed by the High Court in passing the impugned order.

The learned counsel appearing for the State also supported the impugned order Shweta Belwal vs The State Of Uttarakhand on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97514936/
1 passed by the High Court.

sentences.text: 7 Having gone through the impugned order passed by the High Court, we have no hesitation in observing that the same is a non speaking order.
Except referring to few decisions of this Court, the High Court has not discussed anything in its impugned order.
It was expected of the High Court to at least give a fair idea as to what is the case of the prosecution.
It was also expected of the High Court to record the submissions that must have been canvassed on behalf of the appellant herein.
On this short ground alone, we propose to set aside the impugned order and remit the matter to the High Court for fresh consideration.
8 The impugned order is accordingly set aside.
The matter is remitted to the High Court.
Criminal Miscellaneous Application No 1511 of 2021 filed before the High Court is ordered to be restored to its original file.
9 The High Court shall give priority to the matter and decide afresh by way of a speaking order.
We clarify at this stage that we have not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
10 The interim order passed by this Court shall continue till the disposal of the matter before the High Court.
11 The appeal is accordingly disposed of.
12 Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
